text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An American company, among four firms vying to replace Namibia's presidential jet, the Falcon 900, is lobbying hard behind the scenes, offering government a tantalising "discount" of close to 70 million Namibian dollars. The winning tender is expected to be announced within the next two weeks.

- The Namibia National Woamen's Organisation (Nanawo) has called on men and women to wear black on Thursday, the day on which Nangombe Kalukambe, 24, appears in court at Tsumeb on charges relating to the rape of a two-year-old infant. Nanawo has made the call to protest the continued violence against defenceless women and children.

- The Ministry of Mines and Energy has questioned the status of Himba headman Hikuminue Kapika and alleged that the Himba leader is part of a "well organised faced aimed at perpetuating European preconceptions and stereotypes about Africa." The statement follows the start of an European tour of two Himba leaders to protest against the proposed Epupa hydro-electric scheme. The statement signed by the acting permanent secretary in the ministry, Inge Zaamwani, further accused Kapika of being a tool of enviromental extremists in the West, who did not want meaningful development to take place in developing countries.
